conditions.description: European Postdoctoral Fellowships are open to researchers of any nationality who wish to engage in R&I projects by coming to Europe from any country in the world or by moving within Europe.

Global Postdoctoral Fellowships are open to European nationals or long-term residents. The specific definition of long-term residents is referenced in the footnotes and described in the eligibility conditions at the end of the Work Programme part.

Applications must be made jointly by the researcher and a beneficiary in the academic or non-academic sector. Financial and operational capacity requirements for beneficiaries are described in Annex C of the Work Programme General Annexes.

Specific eligibility conditions apply to MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships in research areas covered by the Euratom Research and Training Programme; these are described at the end of the Work Programme part.

Organisations eligible for Euratom-funded MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships must be active in nuclear research and established in an EU Member State or a country associated to the Euratom Research and Training Programme.

The non-academic sector placement host organisation must be established in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country (or, for Euratom-area proposals, in an EU Member State or Euratom-associated country). A researcher recruited from the non-academic sector must undertake any non-academic placement at a different non-academic host organisation.

Eligible countries for participation are described in Annex B of the Work Programme General Annexes. Certain non-EU/non-Associated Countries have made specific provisions for making funding available for their participants in Horizon Europe projects.

Proposals must conform to admissibility conditions described in Annex A and Annex E of the Horizon Europe Work Programme General Annexes, including proposal page limits and layout described in Part B of the Application Form available in the Submission System.
